scope: Pure-System production C# plan/parser and exact extracted Editor regression methods; public Qwen planning only. No Unity/GPU/service launched and no motion request sent by this agent. Parent runs actual execution separately.

palm-normal wrist axis requires a palm goal for each moving hand

cpuChecks.compiler: Unity-bundled Mono C# compiler, actual production files, not UnityEngine or parser stubs
cpuChecks.unityExecution: Parent scheduled separately; not claimed by this report

interpretationChanges: Run 1 used fixed default elbows; later runs derive elbow auto-solving when unspecified. Thus run-level parameter-match counts cannot be compared as a shared success metric. All public user prompts remain identical; synthetic DTOs gain the new false-default internal fields.

firstRealPlanFixture.rawTagSelection: Case zh-forward-greeting selected before results; original first-run tag preserved exactly. New parser exports BendAuto=true. No manual elbow/axis/amplitude or seed edits. Version-1 fixed-default interpretation remains archived.

finalIndependentFindings.finding: Single-arm forward posture is repeatedly lost to the basic right-wave route.
Requested lateral static palm display becomes forward motion with an unnecessary local wrist wave; spoken text claims lateral despite the tag.
Final contract omits both palm attributes while selecting palm-normal; the production validator correctly rejects the tag.
Final restored contract still routes the previously supported free dance to compose and emits cycles=4; the production validator rejects it. Free-generate regression remains unresolved.

Final run retains explicit zero elbow angles and does not turn on Auto, but explains the failed wave then retries a static palm goal under the same arm constraints. Do not count this as achieved reachability or a complete refusal.
The first-run shake-head plus correct limitation explanation is a reasonable refusal, despite the narrow original route expectation; do not force none just to improve the score.

conclusion: The new representation can express palm orientation and leave unspecified elbow geometry to the executor, but autonomous routing, static-versus-moving intent and retention of explicit constraints remain unreliable in these development cases. Neither universal natural intent completion nor non-regression of free generated motion is established.
